subject: OpsLytics — unit economics deep-dive & next evaluation steps
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@opslytics.ai>

Thanks for the walkthrough today, Vanessa — the demo helped clarify latency guarantees. A few follow-ups on economics that our infra lead needs before we move to a PoC: 

- Can you provide a per-1M token cost comparison to the major hyperscalers for a 7B/13B family model, both with and without quantization?
- How much do batching and a ~70% KV-prefix cache hit rate typically reduce per-token cost in your deployments?
- We want a short test plan (scripts/inputs) we can run on our side to reproduce costs.

We also attached the template we use internally for TCO so you can populate it. Proposed next step: a focused benchmark with your guidance next week.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Product 
OpsLytics
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@opslytics.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — cost questions and next tests

Emily — great questions, thanks. Short answers up front, then a proposed plan below.

Quick summary:
- Baseline per-1M tokens (in hosted API) for 13B FP16: ~ $120–$170 vs hyperscaler managed endpoints typically quoted at $160–$240 depending on instance type & reserved commit. Quantized endpoints (8-bit/4-bit) reduce our unit cost ~35–55% depending on model family and quality target.
- Batching: moving from single-request (no batching) to continuous batching at 16–32 effective batch size lowers cost by ~20–35% for steady-state traffic; larger batches yield diminishing latency returns for your interactive use-case.
- KV-prefix cache: 70% cache hit rate in a typical assistant-style workload reduces tokens issued to the model by a like percentage for repeated prefixes — net token spend drops linearly with hit rate when cacheable prefixes dominate. In practice this translates to ~25–40% unit cost savings on mixed conversational workloads.

Proposed experiment (3-stage, 10 business day cadence):
1) Baseline capture (OpsLytics): run a 200k-token script collected from your real interactions; return raw logs (latency, tokens, prefix lengths). (2 business days)
2) Redwood-managed run: we run same script against our hosted API variants (FP16, 8-bit quant, 4-bit quant) with no cache and then with simulated prefix caching at 70% hit. We capture per-request latency, tail percentiles, and token counts. (3 business days)
3) Hyperscaler parity run: OpsLytics runs same script against your hyperscaler-of-choice (we’ll provide the command-line invocation and expected instance sizing) and returns logs. Redwood will help interpret diffs and normalize for instance sizing. (3 business days)

Deliverables: populated per-1M token economics spreadsheet, a small slide deck summarizing variance drivers (batching, cache, quantization), and recommended config for your PoC.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short test-plan PDF and a pre-filled econ matrix to speed this up.

Next steps: if this plan looks good, can we lock in a kickoff on Monday 2/15 at 10am PT to run stage 1? Rishi and Marissa will own the Redwood side of the runs.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — cost questions and next tests

Emily — we’re set for the kickoff at 10am PT. A couple clarifications from the sales side so we scope correctly: 

- For the hyperscaler run, can you confirm which cloud/instance family you plan to use? (G5/Inferentia/A100 equivalents make a big difference in the normalization.)
- Please include a short sample of the 200k-token script (20–30 lines) so we can sanity-check tokenization and expected prefix reuse.
- We can include an optional Dedicated capacity estimate if the normalized run shows sustained savings — Marissa, can you draft a committed-capacity comparison slide (monthly commit vs per-token) and drop it in the shared Drive by EOD Tue?

Also looping in Marissa for the committed numbers and to capture any procurement constraints on your side.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@opslytics.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — cost questions and next tests

Thanks — confirmed. We’ll run the baseline script against GCP A100 (n1-standard equivalent) and will upload a masked 50k-token sample by EOD today (privacy redacted). A couple of asks from our infra/security team: 

- Can Redwood share the exact quantization knobs you suggest (per-channel vs per-tensor, activation quantization off/on) so our run is comparable?
- Our security lead also asked about telemetry: what metadata does Redwood collect during the hosted-run (IP, prompt hashes, free-text logging)? We want to ensure we can map that to our privacy policy.

We’ll also accept the Dedicated estimate later if the numbers show a >25% savings. Looking forward to Monday’s kickoff.

Emily
Head of Product 
OpsLytics
